newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CDL Investments sees more growth in 97/8.
newsitem.headline: CDL Investments sees more growth in 97/8.

text.p: CDL Investments Ltd on Wednesday said it expected calendar 1997 and 1998 to show further growth in turnover and profitability but that the first half of the current year was unlikely to show an improvement.
Chairman Bruce Davidson told the annual meeting that the company was paying tax in the current year for the first time.
The impact of this, plus the timing of its 1997 projects, meant the first six months was unlikely to show any improvement over the same 1996 period.
"The second six months is when we expect to achieve the significant portion of our 1997 profitability," he said.
"We expect the full year's results to show further growth in both turnover and net profit after tax and for this trend to continue in 1998," he said.
In calendar 1996, CDL Investment's net profit after tax was NZ$9.09 million, up from $6.67 million a year earlier.
CDL Investments is a unit of City Developments Ltd , which itself is a unit of the Hong Leong Group.
City Developments is Singapore's the largest publicly-listed property investor and developer.
CDL Investments also forms part of CDL Hotels New Zealand Ltd.

Davidson said CDL Land's activities would continue to represent the bulk of CDL Investments' profile in terms of the level of capital and asset commitment and its continued strong profit contribution.
"The company has established a strong earnings base and the objective now is to build on this base to develop continued earnings growth over time," he said.
"We will continue to seek to add to our land bank within the key growth areas identified to enhance our long term profitability," he said.
The company would continue to maintain a strong balance sheet and a conservative debt-equity ratio, he said.
CDL Investments last traded at NZ$0.41, up one cent.
